question: How do I use a canonical URL for a republished article? Does it redirect visitors or change the sitemap?
expected: canonical_url absoluteHTTP(S)/sitepath; no redirect; sitemap false excludesduplicate actualURL.

result.answer:
To use a canonical URL for an article, set the `canonical_url` field in the article's front matter to the desired HTTP(S) or `/site-path`.

Regarding your other questions:
*   **Redirects:** It does not redirect visitors; it provides a link for metadata and feeds.
*   **Sitemap:** It does not change the sitemap. While `jekyll-sitemap` uses the actual URL, you can exclude a page from the sitemap by setting `sitemap: false`.

Note that same-domain canonical paths (such as www/non-www equivalents) are preferred, as cross-domain canonicals are ignored in favor of the browser path.

Sources:
* [Page metadata and article images](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#seo-metadata)
* [Canonical article](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/62-canonical-article)

question: How do I make my personal blog publisher a Person? Will it replace a guest author, and do I need a logo?
expected: Since v2.1.0. Default/fallback is Organization, not Person. Explicitly set type: Person in the existing publisher mapping, preserving fields and avoiding duplicates. Person ignores logo and uses image/site avatar. Publish/check JSON-LD publisher on home/post, URLs with baseurl; guest article authors unchanged. Does not guarantee search appearance.

result.answer:
To set your publisher as a Person, you must explicitly set `publisher.type: Person` within your existing publisher mapping in `_config.yml`.

*   **Logo/Image:** A Person uses an `image` and ignores the `logo` field.
*   **Guest Authors:** This change does not replace a guest author. Page-level guest authors do not inherit the site author's URL, and article authors remain unchanged.

```yaml
publisher:
  type: Person
  name: "Your Name"
  url: "https://example.com"
  image: "/assets/img/profile.jpg"
```

**Next Step:** Verify the published `application/ld+json` publisher metadata to ensure the change is active.

Sources:
* [Publisher setup](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/60-person-publisher)
* [Publisher, analytics and icon configuration](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config)

question: How do I republish an article while pointing to the original, and exclude the copy from my sitemap? Will visitors be redirected?
expected: Merge canonical_url original absolute HTTP(S) URL into existing front matter; preserve copy permalink/content. No redirect; metadata/feed links change. With jekyll-sitemap sitemap: false excludes copy actual URL; canonical alone does not. Check published source canonical/og:url/JSON-LD, feed entry and sitemap; preserve per-page pagination canonicals.

result.answer:
To point an article to an original version and exclude the copy from your sitemap, use the `canonical_url` and `sitemap` settings in your article's front matter.

```yaml
---
layout: default
canonical_url: https://example.com/original-article/
sitemap: false
---
```

*   **`canonical_url`**: Specifies the HTTP(S) or `/site-path` of the original. This provides a link for metadata and feeds.
*   **`sitemap: false`**: Excludes this specific page from the sitemap (note that `jekyll-sitemap` uses the actual URL; setting this to `false` prevents the copy from being listed).
*   **Redirects**: No, `canonical_url` does not perform a redirect; it only provides metadata/feed links.

Sources:
* [SEO Metadata and Canonical URLs](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#seo-metadata)
* [Search Visibility](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/65-search-visibility)

question: How do I set a post sharing image and article illustration without changing its visible heading or inserting a photograph into the body?
expected: Edit existing description/og_title/og_image/og_image_alt/schema_image; real uploaded image; preserve title. Social and BlogPosting image roles separate; no crops/inspection. Check generated tags/JSON and image URL/baseurl; no guaranteed preview or ranking.

result.answer:
To set a post sharing image and an article illustration without changing the visible heading or adding content to the body, use the following metadata in your post's front matter:

*   **`og_image`**: Sets the social sharing image.
*   **`header_img`**: Sets the visible article illustration (header image).
*   **`schema_image`**: Sets the image for the post's JSON-LD (BlogPosting) metadata.

Note that `title` controls the visible heading; leaving it unchanged preserves your current heading.

```yaml
---
layout: default
header_type: post
title: "My existing heading"
og_image: {{ '/assets/img/social.jpg' | relative_url }}
header_img: {{ '/assets/img/header.jpg' | relative_url }}
schema_image: {{ '/assets/img/schema.jpg' | relative_url }}
---
```

**Next Step:** Verify the images appear correctly on narrow screens and in social previews.

Sources:
* [SEO Metadata](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#seo-metadata)
* [Article Images](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#article-images)
* [Post Sharing](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/64-post-sharing)

question: Can I hide my auxiliary page from crawlers, sitemap and local search just with noindex? What about Algolia?
expected: Independent robots noindex follow, sitemap false with jekyll-sitemap, include_on_search false for Lunr/Fuse/Simple search; Algolia files_to_exclude and reupload. Public page remains accessible, no robots.txt block preventing noindex read; verify published metadata/sitemap/search. No automatic exclusions or instant crawler removal.

result.answer:
No. Using `robots: "noindex, follow"` only controls crawlers and does not change your local search index or sitemap. To exclude a page from the sitemap, you must set `sitemap: false`.

For Algolia, `include_on_search: false` in the document front matter affects ranking via `customRanking`, but it does not exclude the file from the index. To exclude files from Algolia, use `algolia.files_to_exclude`.

Relevant sources:
* [SEO controls](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/65-search-visibility)
* [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)
* [Algolia search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/37-algolia-search)

**Next step:** Update your page's front matter with the specific exclusion settings required for each service.
